== REQUESTS: How big is each pod?

[F1] CONTEXT  vpa-min-allowed  StatefulSet/ml/trainer
    VPA trainer's minAllowed keeps its recommendation above what usage suggests: the uncapped target is lower.
    What it means: A configured floor, not usage, sets these requests.
    Confidence: high
    Evidence:
      - VerticalPodAutoscaler/ml/trainer .spec.resourcePolicy.containerPolicies[*].minAllowed.cpu = 2
      - VerticalPodAutoscaler/ml/trainer .status.recommendation.containerRecommendations[trainer].uncappedTarget.cpu = 500m
      - VerticalPodAutoscaler/ml/trainer .spec.resourcePolicy.containerPolicies[*].minAllowed.memory = 8Gi
      - VerticalPodAutoscaler/ml/trainer .status.recommendation.containerRecommendations[trainer].uncappedTarget.memory = 3Gi

== POLICY: Where may they run, and may they move?

[F2] BLOCKER  no-room-elsewhere  Pod/ml/trainer-0
    None of the 3 other schedulable node(s) in the snapshot can take this pod. Draining this node would leave it Pending, so autoscalers keep the node.
    What it means: The other nodes say no because of: node selector on 3 node(s).
    Applies to: cluster-autoscaler, karpenter
    Confidence: medium
    Evidence:
      - Pod/ml/trainer-0 requests (containers, init containers, overhead) = cpu=2 memory=8Gi
      - Pod/ml/trainer-0 .spec.nodeSelector = team=ml
      - Node/general-a fit check = node selector team=ml not matched
      - Node/general-b fit check = node selector team=ml not matched
      - Node/general-c fit check = node selector team=ml not matched
    Other explanations:
      - Karpenter may replace this node with a cheaper one instead of deleting it; this rule only checks moving pods onto existing nodes.
      - Requests may be larger than real usage; right-sizing (for example with VPA recommendations) could create room.
    Unknowns:
      - Placement is a first-fit estimate by requests, largest pod first; a different packing might succeed.
      - Volume zones, pod priority and preemption were not evaluated.

== NODES: Will the node autoscaler remove or replace the node?

[F3] BLOCKER  karpenter-consolidation-policy  Node/ml-a
    NodePool ml only consolidates empty nodes (consolidationPolicy WhenEmpty). This node runs 1 pod(s) that would need to move, so Karpenter will not remove or replace it for being underused.
    Applies to: karpenter
    Confidence: high
    Evidence:
      - NodePool/ml .spec.disruption.consolidationPolicy = WhenEmpty
      - Node/ml-a .metadata.labels["karpenter.sh/nodepool"] = ml
    Other explanations:
      - Expiry or drift can still replace the node, depending on the NodePool's other settings.

Limitations:
  - Snapshot heuristic, not a scheduler simulation: placement checks cover node selectors, required node affinity, taints, required pod (anti-)affinity, topology spread and host ports, but not volume zones, priorities, preemption or preferred rules.
  - Autoscaler settings are read where the cluster exposes them (Karpenter NodePools and NodeClaims), not Cluster Autoscaler flags or node group minimums.
  - One point in time: PDB status, replica counts and events change.
  - Packing is measured with resource requests, not real usage.
  - Pod size is judged only where a VPA recommendation exists; other workloads are unknowns.
  - Read-only: KubeShrink never modifies a cluster.
